title: RRULE expansion loses TZID — recurring events at fixed local time misalign across DST
description: src/ics/rrule.rs:22-26 builds the rrule input as 'DTSTART:<utc>Z\nRRULE:...'. The dtstart parameter is already DateTime<Utc>, so the original TZID (e.g. America/New_York) is gone by the time it reaches the rrule crate. For an event that recurs at '9am New York time', occurrences pre- and post-DST land on different UTC hours; expanding from a fixed UTC DTSTART produces instances that drift by an hour across DST transitions. The rrule crate supports 'DTSTART;TZID=America/New_York:20200101T090000' — we should plumb the original TZID/local time through expand_rrule rather than collapsing to UTC up-front.
acceptance_criteria: Recurring weekly event with TZID=America/New_York at 09:00 local time produces instances at 09:00 New York time on each side of a DST transition (i.e., 13:00 UTC during EST and 13:00 UTC during EDT — wait, that's 14:00 EST → 13:00 EDT in UTC; verify direction). Add a test that expands such an event across a DST boundary and asserts local-time alignment.
close_reason: Plumbed dtstart_tz: Option<chrono_tz::Tz> through EventSummary and into expand_rrule; expansion now feeds the rrule crate a 'DTSTART;TZID=<name>:<local-time>' header for TZID-anchored events, so iteration happens in local time and DST transitions land at the correct UTC offset. Falls back to UTC DTSTART for floating/UTC events. New tests: weekly NY-anchored event across spring 2026 DST asserts pre-DST 14:00 UTC and post-DST 13:00 UTC (both 09:00 NY local), plus a regression test pinning the UTC-only fallback path.

title: search_events drops DESCRIPTION/LOCATION matches when server returns any SUMMARY hits
description: In src/server.rs:271-282, search_events sends a server-side calendar-query whose prop-filter only matches against SUMMARY (see xml.rs:159-161 text_search_body). If the server returns ANY matches, the code uses just that subset and never falls back to the broad calendar-query + client-side filter. Events whose query term appears only in DESCRIPTION or LOCATION are silently dropped. The spec (docs/00-spec.md §4 search_events) explicitly requires matching SUMMARY *and* DESCRIPTION on the client-side fallback, so the current narrowing violates the spec.
acceptance_criteria: search_events returns events that match in any of SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION, or LOCATION. Add tests for: (a) match-in-summary, (b) match-only-in-description, (c) match-only-in-location. Likely simplest fix: skip the server-side prop-filter and always do the broad fetch + client-side filter (or merge both result sets).
close_reason: Dropped server-side SUMMARY-only prop-filter; search_events now always fetches the date window and filters client-side via EventSummary::matches_query, which checks SUMMARY, DESCRIPTION, and LOCATION case-insensitively. Added 7 matcher tests + 2 parser tests covering all three match cases and a regression case for cross-field false positives.

title: Floating ICS times treated as UTC instead of local
description: src/ics/timezone.rs:101-103 falls back to 'Utc.from_utc_datetime(&naive)' for DTSTART/DTEND values without a Z suffix and without a TZID. Per RFC 5545 §3.3.5, that is *floating* time — the wall-clock time at the location of the user. Treating it as UTC means floating events display at the wrong time for users not in UTC. Fix: either resolve to the system local timezone, or surface the 'floating' nature in the EventSummary so callers can interpret it correctly.
acceptance_criteria: An ICS DTSTART of '20260503T090000' (no Z, no TZID) rendered for a user in America/Los_Angeles shows '09:00 local', not '02:00 local' (which is what UTC->LA conversion produces). Add a test.

title: All-day events render as midnight UTC instead of an all-day marker
description: src/ics/timezone.rs:113-116 parses VALUE=DATE all-day events as midnight UTC. The DateTime<Utc> then flows through the same display formatting as timed events ('YYYY-MM-DD 00:00 UTC'), which is misleading: the event is 'all day on 2026-05-03', not 'starting at midnight UTC on 2026-05-03'. For users in negative-UTC offsets (e.g. America/Los_Angeles), the local-time conversion shifts the displayed date to the day before. Need a way to mark all-day events and format them differently in EventSummary/EventDetail Display impls.
acceptance_criteria: An all-day event on 2026-05-03 displayed for a user in America/Los_Angeles shows '2026-05-03 (all day)' rather than '2026-05-02 17:00 PDT'.

title: EXDATE / RDATE / RECURRENCE-ID overrides are ignored during RRULE expansion
description: src/server.rs:191-225 expands recurring events using only the master RRULE. ICS files commonly include: EXDATE (cancelled instances), RDATE (extra occurrences outside the rule), and additional VEVENTs with RECURRENCE-ID (modified single instances). The current expand_rrule path reads only the master RRULE, so cancelled instances still appear, and modified instances appear with the master's properties. The rrule crate's RRuleSet supports rdate/exdate; we just need to pass them in. RECURRENCE-ID overrides require post-processing the expanded set to substitute or remove instances.
acceptance_criteria: Given an ICS with RRULE plus an EXDATE for 2026-05-03, expand_rrule for that day returns an empty set. Given an ICS with a RECURRENCE-ID override that changes the summary on 2026-05-03, the expanded instance for that date carries the override's summary. Add tests for both.
close_reason: Added extract_recurrence_modifiers helper in server.rs that pulls EXDATE/RDATE from the master VEVENT and converts each override VEVENT's RECURRENCE-ID to a synthetic EXDATE. expand_rrule now accepts an extra_lines: &[String] argument and concatenates these onto the rrule input string the crate already understands. list_events passes the extracted lines through. Tests: RDATE injects a date outside the master pattern (the suspected cause of two missing recurring events on a non-pattern day), EXDATE excludes a specific instance, synthetic EXDATE from RECURRENCE-ID prevents master+override double-emit. Plus 4 server-side tests for the extractor across vanilla, override, TZID, and empty-modifier cases. 24 tests total, clippy clean.

title: list_events range uses UTC midnight, can clip events for non-UTC users
description: In src/server.rs:172-173, list_events constructs the time-range as start=00:00:00 UTC and end=23:59:59 UTC of the requested dates. For users east of UTC, late-evening local events on the requested last day fall after 23:59 UTC and are excluded; for users west of UTC, early-morning local events on the requested first day fall before 00:00 UTC and are also excluded. Conversely, events from the day before/after may be incorrectly included.
acceptance_criteria: Range computation accepts (or infers) the user's local timezone, and an event scheduled for 22:00 local time on the last day of the requested range is included regardless of UTC offset. Add a regression test.
notes: Discovered while fixing the RRULE 500-cap bug in src/ics/rrule.rs (recurring events not appearing in list_events). Same code path.
close_reason: list_events / search_events / dump_raw_calendar_data accept an optional timezone: Option<String> (IANA name, e.g. 'America/Toronto'); start_date and end_date are now interpreted as INCLUSIVE local-day boundaries in that timezone (or chrono::Local if omitted) and converted to a half-open UTC window [00:00 local, 00:00 next-day local). Also fixed a latent off-by-one: to_caldav_timestamp previously used <end_date>T000000Z for the end attribute, so a single-day query (start==end) produced an empty CalDAV time-range. New helpers: parse_timezone_arg, local_day_window_to_utc, resolve_local_to_utc; to_caldav_timestamp now takes DateTime<Utc>. 6 new tests covering Toronto evening, Tokyo east-of-UTC morning, multi-day inclusive end, DST spring-forward, invalid TZ rejection, and CalDAV timestamp format. 36 tests pass, clippy clean.

title: Test coverage gaps: parser, xml, server routing, timezone fallbacks
description: Aside from the 3 rrule tests added in this branch, there is no test coverage for: parser.rs (icalendar primary, regex fallback, all-day/floating/UTC datetime cases), xml.rs (multistatus parsing, partial-failure handling), server.rs (find_client_for_url, extract_host, parse_date), and timezone.rs (resolve_timezone aliases, parse_datetime branches). Add a test module per file covering the stable behaviors.
acceptance_criteria: cargo test reports >= 20 tests across the listed files. CI green.

title: extract_rrule_from_ics picks first RRULE in the ICS, may not be the master's
description: src/server.rs:364-372 returns the first 'RRULE:' line found in the raw ICS. When an ICS contains the master VEVENT plus RECURRENCE-ID overrides, parse_events may yield multiple EventSummary entries; the loop at server.rs:191 then applies the same first-RRULE to every recurring event in that ICS. For a master event whose override has a different RRULE (rare, but legal under RFC 5545), or for ICS resources where the master is not the first VEVENT, this produces wrong expansions. Should look up the RRULE from the matching VEVENT's parsed properties rather than scanning the raw text.
acceptance_criteria: Replace the regex-based extract_rrule_from_ics with a per-event RRULE lookup carried on EventSummary (or EventDetail). Existing tests still pass.
close_reason: Root cause of the user-visible 'recurring events missing from list_events' symptom on Fastmail (Toronto): VTIMEZONE STANDARD/DAYLIGHT components carry their own RRULEs describing DST transitions, and extract_rrule_from_ics scanned the entire ICS so it returned the VTIMEZONE STANDARD's 'FREQ=YEARLY;BYMONTH=11;BYDAY=1SU' instead of the VEVENT's 'FREQ=WEEKLY'. expand_rrule then produced zero instances in any non-November window and the events vanished. Fix: extract_rrule_from_ics now scopes the search to VEVENT blocks and returns the master's RRULE (the VEVENT with RRULE and no RECURRENCE-ID), skipping VTIMEZONE/STANDARD/DAYLIGHT and override RRULEs. Added 4 regression tests including a real-shape Fastmail ICS and an end-to-end Ozempic weekly-from-2024 expansion into a 2026 window.

title: Unrecognized HTTP statuses surface as XmlParseError
description: src/dav/client.rs:105 returns 'CalDavError::XmlParseError(format!("unexpected HTTP {status} for {url}"))' when an unmapped HTTP status is received (e.g. 500, 502, 504). That misclassifies network/server errors as parse errors — breaks observability and any caller that branches on error type. Add a CalDavError::Http variant or generic CalDavError::Server(String, StatusCode) and use it here.
acceptance_criteria: A 500 response from the CalDAV server is reported as a server/HTTP error, not an XML parse error. Update from_http_status mapping if needed and add a test.

title: DTEND default duration falls back to 1 hour instead of RFC 5545 default
description: src/server.rs:194-196 uses 'event.dtend.map(|e| e - event.dtstart).unwrap_or(Duration::hours(1))' when DTEND is missing. Per RFC 5545 §3.6.1, missing DTEND means the event has the duration of DTSTART itself: zero for DATE-TIME, or one day for VALUE=DATE. The current 1-hour heuristic is a guess. Also: VEVENTs may carry DURATION instead of DTEND (RFC 5545); we currently ignore DURATION.
acceptance_criteria: expand_rrule honors DURATION when present, defaults to zero-length for missing DTEND on a DATE-TIME event, and defaults to one day for VALUE=DATE all-day events. Add tests.

title: display_tz selection from VTIMEZONE map is non-deterministic
description: src/server.rs:199 and src/ics/parser.rs:82 pick display_tz via 'tz_map.values().next().copied()'. tz_map is a HashMap, so iteration order is randomized per process run. For an ICS with multiple VTIMEZONE blocks (e.g. one for DTSTART and one for DTEND, or imported events from mixed sources), the displayed local time can flip across runs. Should pick the TZID associated with the event's DTSTART specifically, falling back to system local if absent.
acceptance_criteria: Given an ICS with two VTIMEZONE blocks (America/New_York and Europe/Berlin) where DTSTART has TZID=America/New_York, the rendered local_start always shows in New York time across repeated runs. Add a test that constructs such an ICS and asserts the timezone.
close_reason: Incidentally fixed while implementing jfr. parse_events_icalendar / parse_events_fallback / parse_details_icalendar / parse_details_fallback now resolve display_tz per-event from the DTSTART's TZID parameter (with VTIMEZONE map lookup and IANA fallback), instead of HashMap.values().next(). server.rs:list_events likewise uses event.dtstart_tz for display. Added a parser test with two VTIMEZONE blocks (America/New_York and Europe/Berlin) where DTSTART references NY — local_start is rendered in NY, never Berlin.

title: No example config file or schema documentation
description: Users can only learn the expected config schema by reading src/config.rs. Add a config.example.toml at the repo root (referenced from the README, when one exists) showing each AuthType variant and its required credentials fields. Reference the path resolution rules (, ~/.config/mcp-caldav/config.toml).
acceptance_criteria: config.example.toml exists with at least one example per AuthType (Basic, AppPassword, OAuth2). README — or the spec doc — links to it.

title: expand_rrule has 10 args (clippy::too_many_arguments) — refactor to ExpandRequest struct
description: src/ics/rrule.rs:9-20 takes 10 positional arguments. Clippy flags this and the call site in server.rs:201-212 is hard to read. Refactor to a struct (e.g. ExpandRequest) containing rrule_str, dtstart, duration, range bounds, summary, master_uid, location, description, display_tz.
acceptance_criteria: expand_rrule takes one struct argument. Clippy too_many_arguments warning is gone (no #[allow]). Existing tests still pass.

title: find_client_for_url host-only fallback can route to wrong account when two accounts share a host
description: src/server.rs:84-99 first matches accounts by base_url prefix, then falls back to host-only match. With two accounts on the same host (e.g. two iCloud accounts), host-fallback returns whichever client iterates first from HashMap.values() — non-deterministic and potentially wrong. Auth credentials may then be applied to a calendar URL that belongs to a different account. Should require base_url prefix match strictly, or pick the longest-prefix match if multiple candidates exist.
acceptance_criteria: Configure two accounts on the same host with distinct path prefixes; calendar URLs are routed to the correct account in 100% of runs. Add a test using HashMap construction order shuffled.
